title: Appeal packets for Medicare Advantage admission denials at freestanding rehab hospitals (IRFs) and long-term care hospitals (LTCHs)

fixture.label: queue #11 benchmark case R1: a real opportunity from queue #10 (H2); the appetite is a test fixture

upstream_status.summary: Lead hypothesis H2 since 2026-10-02. Queue #10 (2026-10-03): not validated; no original deal-breaker failed; one open fatal unknown (winnability of unappealed denials); ranked first as a test only. The owner's market, test and contact decision is pending.

buyer: Freestanding inpatient rehabilitation facilities (IRFs) first, then long-term care hospitals (LTCHs); not units inside acute hospitals
user: The facility's admissions, intake or utilization-review staff (for example a managed-care specialist) who build and file appeals
job: When a Medicare Advantage plan denies a patient's admission before the stay (a pre-service denial), build a same-day appeal packet that sets the patient's clinical facts against the payer's own admission criteria, for the facility's own staff to review and file through the payer portal or fax they already use. No prior-authorization submission; the product does not file anything.

evidence.claim: KFF (2026): Medicare Advantage plans deny 54% of IRF and 65% of LTCH admission requests, against under 8% for all services.
evidence.quote: MA plans deny 54% of IRF and 65% of LTCH admission requests, against under 8% for all services
evidence.source: Product role's evidence summary of KFF (2026) in ~/temper-ai/workspaces/product/compare-10-desk-c1/state/desk/input.md

evidence.claim: KFF, describing OIG data: only 36% of LTCH and 31% of IRF admission denials were appealed, so about two-thirds were never reviewed on appeal.
evidence.quote: which happened for 36% of LTCH denials, 31% of IRF denials, and 18% of SNF denials

evidence.claim: HHS OIG (OEI-09-24-00330, June 2024 data, 19 MA organizations): of the denials that were appealed, plans overturned 43% for IRFs and 36% for LTCHs. Appealed denials only; unappealed denials are not measured.
evidence.quote: When enrollees appealed, MAOs collectively overturned 36 percent of LTCH denials and 43 percent of IRF denials, indicating that some enrollees were initially denied medically necessary care.

evidence.claim: OIG: IRF overturn rates on appeal ranged by plan from 14% to 86%, so winnability depends heavily on the payer.
evidence.quote: For example, IRF overturn rates ranged by MAO from 14 percent to 86 percent.

evidence.claim: AMRPA's member survey (367 IRFs, July-August 2024): 3,866 of more than 15,000 initial MA denials were appealed at the plan reconsideration level (24.8%).
evidence.quote: 3,866 were appealed at "Level 1" (the plan reconsideration level). This represents an appeal rate of 24.8%

evidence.claim: AMRPA says MA admission determinations are hard to challenge because appeals add days. The work exists; no fee for outside help is reported.
evidence.quote: These determinations are difficult to challenge, since subsequent appeals take additional days

evidence.claim: AMRPA describes appeals beyond the plan level as lengthy and time-consuming for IRF admissions (burden asserted, not measured in time or cost).
evidence.quote: this level of appeal is rarely utilized for patients seeking admission to an IRF given the lengthy and time-consuming process

evidence.claim: Northeast Rehabilitation Hospital, a freestanding IRF, says its own Managed Care Specialist runs MA denial appeals: the job is done in-house there, with no vendor named.
evidence.quote: If our Managed Care Specialist disagrees with the Medicare Advantage findings, and believes that you or your loved one are still a candidate for inpatient rehabilitation

evidence.claim: OIG work plan SRS-E-26-004: a medical-record review that would measure how many denied post-acute admission requests met Medicare coverage rules is planned, not published.
evidence.quote: We will also conduct medical record reviews for a sample of cases to determine the extent to which MAOs denied requests for post-acute care admissions that met

evidence.claim: OIG 2022 (all MA prior-authorization denials, all services) named inpatient rehabilitation among services in denials that met coverage rules; no IRF-specific share is given.
evidence.quote: Examples of health care services involved in denials that met Medicare coverage rules included advanced imaging services (e.g., MRIs) and post-acute facility stays (e.g., inpatient rehabilitation).

evidence.claim: Counted from CMS's Medicare Post-Acute Care PUF (FY2024 IRF file, NATION row): $10,822,889,016 total Medicare fee-for-service payment over 434,556 IRF stays, about $24,906 per IRF stay. Staff time per appeal is not measured.

Route to market: about two-thirds of IRFs are hospital units (outside the segment), about 80-100 separate sales in total, and no first buyer or state is chosen.
Are drafted packets accurate and fileable: no made-up facts, and clinicians judge them ready to file? The planned tests (queue #10 K3) are not run and need patient records under a signed BAA.

appetite.note: Test fixture for the queue #11 benchmark: not the owner's appetite and not a market-screening time limit.

constraints.text: No patient data in this work. Any test with patient records needs a signed BAA and the owner's go-ahead.
No contact with facilities, payers or anyone else without the owner's go-ahead; honest tests only (disclosed AI, opt-in contact).
No real money (ads, deposits, paid tools) without the owner's rails and go-ahead.
Before the first paid use: HIPAA business-associate duties and a BAA with each hospital (45 CFR 164.502(e)), plus a BAA with the model host.
The product builds the packet only: the facility's staff review it and file it through the payer portal or fax they already use. No prior-authorization submission.
Segment: freestanding IRFs and LTCHs only, not units inside acute hospitals.

notes: Hypothesis price (the hypothesis's, not an owner decision): a share (about 5%) of each overturned admission, about $1,100 on an average IRF stay. Channel idea (hypothesis): AMRPA and post-acute user groups, medical billing firms second. Planned but not run (queue #10 K3): a shadow test at 1-2 IRFs on 40 consecutive MA admission denials, packets built in parallel and never filed, two blind clinician reviewers; and zero made-up facts in 50 chart-backed drafts. Both need patient records under a signed BAA and the owner's go-ahead.
